  "research_question": "How do different stimulation paradigms affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Bright Visual Only and Combined paradigms showed the highest success rates (78.45% and 77.98% respectively)",
    "Sham stimulation showed markedly worse performance across all metrics with the lowest success rate (27.33%) and highest Time-to-Target (4.68s)",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only showed intermediate performance with similar success rates (67.33% and 68.54%)",
    "Average Speed was highest in Combined stimulation (12.83 units) and lowest in Sham (10.74 units)",
    "Angular dispersion (AD) was highest in Combined stimulation (0.399) and lowest in Sham (0.236)"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Sham vs all active stimulation paradigms: 2.5x lower success rate and 1.8x longer Time-to-Target compared to the best performing paradigms",
    "Bright Visual Only vs Dim Visual Only: 16.6% higher success rate and 20.2% lower Time-to-Target",
    "Combined vs ICMS Only: 13.8% higher success rate and 19.1% lower Time-to-Target"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Active stimulation paradigms significantly improve navigation performance compared to Sham, with visual stimulation (particularly bright visual) showing stronger benefits than ICMS alone. The Combined paradigm demonstrates the most comprehensive performance enhancement across multiple metrics, suggesting synergistic effects of combined stimulation approaches.",
  "limitations": [
    "No statistical testing provided - findings are purely descriptive without p-values or confidence intervals",

    "No information about variance or distribution shape beyond means",
    "Potential confounding factors not accounted for (e.g., mouse-specific effects, trial order)"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct inferential statistical analysis (ANOVA or mixed-effects models) to determine statistical significance of observed differences, while accounting for unequal group sizes and potential mouse-level random effects."
}
